requirements.requirement: The system must compute an appropriateness score for each provider using normalized prescription-to-condition mappings produced by the ingestion pipeline.
The system must compare observed prescribing patterns against expected condition-treatment mappings derived from ICD-10 associations.
The system must normalize appropriateness scores to a consistent scale between 0 and 1.
The system must weight prescription volumes when calculating appropriateness scores.
The system must penalize prescriptions that do not map to any expected condition-treatment pairing.
The system must produce a structured output containing provider NPI, score, and contributing factors.
The system must invoke an LLM to infer condition-treatment relationships when deterministic mappings are missing.
The system must constrain LLM outputs to a predefined schema for condition-treatment mapping.
The system must log LLM inputs and outputs for each inference used in scoring.
The system must assign a confidence score to each LLM-inferred mapping.
The system must incorporate LLM confidence scores into the final appropriateness score weighting.
The system must fallback to deterministic scoring when LLM inference is unavailable.
The system must reject LLM outputs that do not conform to the expected schema.
The system must handle ambiguous drug-to-condition mappings by invoking LLM disambiguation logic.
The system must ensure LLM prompts include sufficient context (drug, condition candidates, metadata) for accurate inference.
The system must cache LLM mapping results to avoid repeated inference for identical inputs.
The system must return a default score of null when no prescribing data is available for a provider.
The system must flag providers with insufficient data volume and exclude them from scoring calculations.
